thread:
harper: Heads-up from sales: BigRetail wants a "low-latency priority lane" for embedding lookups + rerank. They want p95 latency commitments per-route and a monthly burst bucket. 12mo term.
zane: Clarify: they want latency SLOs (p95) rather than hard QPS guarantees? That changes the telemetry and SLA calculus.
milo: Correct. They care about tail latency for search UX. We could offer a Priority Lane that prioritizes scheduling and uses smaller batch windows. MVP could target p95 < 50ms for embeddings at 20 qps.
anya: Product proposal: ship "Priority Lane Pack" SKU. MVP scope: embeddings + rerank routes only; console toggle + per-route SLO field; billing SKU; burst credits as separate purchasable bucket. No generative outputs in MVP.
claire: Ops concerns: p95 SLO needs fine-grained tracing + synthetic probes per-route. Also need isolation so priority traffic doesn't block best-effort. Propose soft-isolation + dynamic preemption policy.
legal-liz: Legal note: avoid absolute "commitment" language. Recommend SLO language like: "we aim to maintain p95 latency <= Xms; failure will result in service credits calculated per month as Y formula". Cap credits to a % of monthly fee.
zane: Pricing asks from sales: three constructs: OnDemand (baseline), Priority (priority scheduling, no formal SLA), Priority+ (priority scheduling + SLO + premium support). Need numbers.
milo: Cost sketch: priority scheduling reduces batching efficiency -> infra delta ~ $9k/mo for 20 qps baseline. Adding strict SLO and support -> add redundancy buffer, call it $22k/mo. Numbers need sensitivity.
anya: To keep delivery tight, MVP will: 1) only support a single embedding model family, 2) quantized weights by default, 3) SLO monitoring + alerting in console, 4) burst bucket capped per month. ETA 7-9 weeks.
claire: Infra work: - priority scheduler lane (2 sprints) - preemption + backpressure rules (1 sprint) - synthetic p95 probes + dashboard (1 sprint) - per-customer burst token accounting (1 sprint). Total ~5 sprints.
zane: For SLA credits calculation: propose formula based on percentage of minutes where p95 exceeded target; credit = min(0.5 * monthly fee, monthly fee * breach_ratio * factor). Legal to sign off.
legal-liz: That formula looks OK directionally. We will draft exact wording and the credit cap. Also include force majeure and scheduled maintenance carveouts.
harper: Sales negotiation levers: - cap monthly burst (e.g., 2M embeddings ops) - fallback to best-effort when burst exhausted - trial pilot with 3 customers for 90 days - 30d cancellation with early-termination fee in first 3 months.
milo: Implementation detail: priority lane will use smaller max-batch (to hit latency) and a separate pool of pre-warmed workers for hot tenants. Need autoscale knobs + cost control.
anya: Launch acceptance checklist: 1) billing SKU + clear pricing bands, 2) console SLO config + dashboard, 3) routing policy + fallback implemented, 4) synthetic p95 monitoring + alerts, 5) runbook + canary plan, 6) legal-approved SLA text and credit schedule.
zane: Sales wants starter numbers to pitch: OnDemand baseline pricing unchanged; Priority: ~$9.5k/mo for 20 qps baseline; Priority+: ~$22k/mo with SLA & 24/7 support. Include burst bucket add-on pricing per million ops.
legal-liz: We'll prepare two contract variants: Hosted (standard) and Private (data residency + KMS clauses). Private will require higher pricing.

anya: I'll draft spec + API flag by end of week.
milo: I'll post cost sensitivity and infra timeline by Friday.
